title: Playfair Mist — Bilingual Pastel Editorial
description: A misty warm-gray editorial portfolio pairing large Playfair-class italic English headings with Noto Sans KR Light Korean subtitles, unified by a soft sky-to-lavender corner gradient blob. Its bilingual numbered TOC, skill speed-bar system, and project key/value meta-column layout set it apart from single-language pastel formats.
philosophy: This template exists for creatives who operate between two languages and refuse to sacrifice elegance for utility. The English section word is the identity — large, italic, unhurried — while the Korean annotation sits beside it as a respectful equal, never a caption. The gradient blob is atmosphere and breath; it bleeds off a corner precisely because it must never compete with type or claim a focal point. Built for quiet review-committee rooms and gallery walkthroughs, it rejects heavy shadow, saturated accent color, and any device that performs confidence rather than demonstrating it.
goodFor: Bilingual Korean-English UX or graphic design portfolios
3–6 featured project pages with structured 목표/기간/기여도/결과 meta columns
University capstone or thesis portfolio submissions requiring quiet authority
Creative directors presenting work in gallery, jury, or committee settings
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews or data-dense investor decks
Single-language audiences unfamiliar with bilingual typographic hierarchy
High-energy brand pitches that require vivid, saturated color to land
Rapid sales presentations where immediate visual impact outweighs considered reading
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the opening page of a museum catalog — unhurried, mist-laden, confident in restraint. A gradient bloom drifts from the top-right corner like soft morning light, dissolving well before the type zone. One dominant italic phrase, one quiet bilingual annotation beneath a hairline, then generous silence — left-anchored and asymmetrically calm. No drop shadows, no decorative flourishes; only the considered weight of type against warm-gray mist.

examples.layoutNotes: The title slide uses a 12-column grid with a generous outer margin of roughly nine percent on all sides, keeping the type zone unhurried. The soft gradient blob bleeds fully off the top-right corner, occupying the upper-right quadrant without crossing into the central type column. English title anchors left across columns one through eight in the upper-center vertical zone; the Korean subtitle sits immediately beneath, sharing the same left edge but at a visibly lighter weight, separated by a single hairline rule. Portfolio identifier or author name is placed bottom-left, flush with the margin baseline; bottom-right holds a minimal folio or remains empty.

examples.promptCore: The slide breathes like a well-lit gallery alcove — unhurried and quietly authoritative, with two languages coexisting at the same visual weight rather than in hierarchy. Compositional rhythm is asymmetric and deliberately sparse: the dominant italic heading commands the left field while the right meta-column offers structured detail in a cooler, lighter register. The gradient blob is pure atmosphere, a soft mist that recedes the moment the eye finds type. Avoid any device that performs confidence — no drop shadows, no vivid accent strokes, no bounding boxes around speed bars; let whitespace and weight contrast do all the persuasion.

examples.layoutNotes: A 12-column grid with deliberate left-weighted asymmetry: the large italic English section heading anchors cols 1–7, with the Korean annotation aligned to its baseline in cols 2–5, treated as a peer rather than a caption. A fine vertical rule separates the body from a narrow key/value meta column (목표 / 기간 / 기여도 / 결과) occupying cols 9–12. The soft gradient blob bleeds off the top-right corner behind all type layers, and a skill speed-bar row runs across the lower third within an 8% outer margin. The folio number sits flush bottom-right, outside any decorative device.
